recommendation: Keep the source-changing commit as-is. It directly implements the published issue disposition in the authoritative Attachment datatype source without introducing the rejected tag mechanism or broader security-policy changes.
issue_request: FHIR-14679 was a Published FHIR-core security change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. The original request asked for a tag warning about executable attachments, but the accepted resolution was to place the existing Binary warning on Attachment.data and Attachment.url.
initial_application: No FHIR-14679-tagged source commit was found in the relevant Attachment/Binary history, and current source/datatypes/attachment.xml lacked the requested warning on Attachment.data and Attachment.url. The Binary warning itself was already present in source/binary/binary-notes.xml from older security work.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Attachment as an active datatype and Binary as an active resource, keeping both source locations in current build scope. Jira searches found only FHIR-14679 for the relevant attachment executable/security terms, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no later conflicting or narrowing evidence.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/attachment.xml comments for Attachment.data and Attachment.url to warn that inline or referenced attachment content is not constrained to safe content types and needs validation against malicious or malformed content before processing.
source_changes: source/datatypes/attachment.xml: added Binary-style validation warning text to Attachment.data and Attachment.url comments.
